title: 17.6 A 100MHz Self-Calibrating RC Oscillator Capable of Clock-Glitch Detection for Hardware Security in a 3nm FinFET Process
problem: On-chip oscillators are needed for SoC security functions (boot-up, external clock attack detection), but existing designs either provide stable clocks without glitch detection or detect glitches without maintaining stability—no prior design achieves both.
motivation: Security vulnerabilities from external clock attacks and the need for external crystal references in boot make on-chip oscillators critical; unified single IP for both stable clocking and glitch detection improves security coverage and reduces design complexity.
method: Self-calibrating RC oscillator in 3nm FinFET with dual-mode operation: stable 100MHz clock generation via self-calibration and hardware-integrated clock-glitch detection circuit that can identify fault injection attacks on critical system clocks.
key_novelty: First RC oscillator design combining stable on-chip clock generation with integrated clock-glitch detection in a single validated security IP, enabling both boot-up independence and real-time attack monitoring.
contributions: Self-calibrating RC oscillator maintaining 100MHz stable operation in 3nm FinFET process
Integrated clock-glitch detection circuit identifying fault injection attacks
Single unified security IP for multiple critical applications (boot, clock monitoring)
3nm FinFET implementation demonstrating modern process compatibility
baselines: Prior stable RC oscillators; prior clock-glitch detection circuits
limitations: Detection latency, false-positive/negative rates, and overhead in terms of area and power consumption not discussed.
primary_theme: Unified on-chip oscillator for stable clocking and security attack detection
